findings.summary: The ComputeEffectiveScale safe-area clamp branch and the resolver tolerant-undefined fallback are not directly unit-tested.
findings.detail: No test dimension triggers the `scale > maximumInsetScale` branch (the tested dimensions keep the clamp from binding), and no test resolves an undefined BadgePosition/BadgeSize through RendererConfigurationResolver to assert the fallback. Both are correct by inspection: the clamp only binds when min(width,height) < 24*scale, in which case the safe area is already empty and the renderer pass-through result is unchanged; the fallback uses Enum.IsDefined and the code-owned default. These are coverage gaps, not correctness defects, and the acceptance criteria are met by other tests.
evidence: BadgeSizePositionTests.cs dimensions (240,600),(320,480),(500,750),(1000,150),(1000,1500),(2000,3000) never bind the clamp

RendererConfigurationResolver.cs ResolvePosition/ResolveSize use Enum.IsDefined with the default fallback; only the undefined-rejection path is tested (RendererConfigurationTests ValidatorRejectsUndefinedBadgePositionAndSize)
findings.recommended_action: Optional: add a tiny-dimension clamp case and an undefined-value resolver-fallback case.
